title: What the Hand Knows
logline: A batik dyer carries a length of cloth between shade, doorway and full sun before deciding a colour is right, while an apprentice waits for the verdict.
human_question: If the same cloth looks like a different colour in every light, which colour is the real one?

premise.story: A working day in a small dyeing workshop, following one commission from vat to finished cloth, told through the dyer's own standards and disagreements.
premise.place: A home-based batik or dye workshop where colour is judged by eye against samples, memory and daylight.
premise.experience: Cloth moved from shade to doorway to full sun, a squint, a pause, a quiet disagreement, and the moment a colour is finally called right.

concept_links.why: Colour is the only kind of matter, of all twenty-eight, that the eye can see at all, and even that arrives as a blend of countless tiny colours that shifts with distance and light; the source says plainly that the 'true colour' is never seen.
The classification of matter as visible or invisible singles out colour as the one visible kind among twenty-eight, which is exactly what a dyer's daily work depends on and tests.

what_camera_could_observe: The cloth moved between shade, doorway and full sun and held against a sample
Dye vats, wax reserve work, and cloth drying on lines
The dyer squinting, stepping back, comparing
A quiet disagreement with an apprentice or customer over whether a colour matches
The finished cloth folded, priced and sent off
what_must_be_real: The dyer's own commissions, standards and real judgement calls. No staged 'moment of decision'; the workshop's actual order book leads.

possible_arc.opening: A colour sample compared against memory before the vat is even mixed.
possible_arc.turn: The same cloth looking different from every angle and every light.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever verdict the dyer actually reaches, and whether the customer agrees.

requirements: An active dyeing or batik workshop with a real commission in progress
Willingness to be filmed making and disputing colour judgements, not just working the wax and dye
Good natural light through the day

suggestions.name: Batik and dye workshops of the Kalutara/Beruwala coastal belt
suggestions.why: This stretch of coast has a long-established batik trade.
suggestions.verify: A specific workshop and its willingness to be filmed are unverified.

risks: Could become a pretty colour montage with no real stake
Temptation to relight or stage the 'moment of judgement'
Craft reduced to illustration rather than a real livelihood
drop_if: No real commission or order to follow during the filming window

connections.note: Both ask what the eye actually receives, and how much of seeing is taken for granted until it fails or is questioned.
Two senses under pressure at once: colour lost to shifting light, sound lost to wind.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
